newsitem.title: USA: Connective says skin drug test positive.
newsitem.headline: Connective says skin drug test positive.

text.p: Connective Therapeutics Inc said Tuesday that results from a Phase I trial of its ConXn showed it had no serious adverse events and improved skin scores.
Skin scores are a measure of skin thickening often used as a clinical endpoint in scleroderma and associated with life-threatening hardening of the skin and internal organs.

The open-label study involved 11 evaluable patients who received continuous subcutaneous infusion of ConXn for 24 weeks at either 25 micrograms per kilogram per day, or 100 micrograms per kilogram per day, or 200 micrograms per kilogram per day, it said.
The company said 10 of the 11 patients showed improvement in skin scores.

"These results support earlier clinical data and are encouraging as we continue to evaluate the product in an ongoing Phase II trial which is fully enrolled and expected to be completed mid-1997," Connective Senior Vice President of Product Development and Operations Scott Harkonen said in a statement.
